At v1.4.0 (48ba499f83d521c4b42b69ea79770650c4959659) logic/jwts.go VerifyHostToken calls jwt.ParseWithClaims then accepts claims on `if token != nil` only (lines 260-265), returning err=nil. golang-jwt/jwt/v4 v4.5.2 Parser.ParseWithClaims returns a non-nil *Token with Valid left false plus a ValidationError on bad signature or expired claims; token.Valid is set true only after signature+claims succeed. Authorize in controllers/node.go:180-186 (v1.4.0) treats VerifyHostToken err==nil as host auth and sets hostIDHeader from attacker-chosen claims.ID. GET /api/v1/host is registered Authorize(true, false, "host", pull) at controllers/hosts.go:48; pull() (hosts.go:188-266) loads that hostID and returns HostPull (Host, Nodes, ServerConfig, Peers, PeerIDs, HostNetworkInfo, EgressRoutes, firewall/gateway state). CVE.org CVE-2026-38651 is PUBLISHED (not rejected); GHSA-qpv2-rwc8-c993 withdrawn_at is null.

findings: CVE-2026-38651 / GHSA-qpv2-rwc8-c993 is a real published host-JWT signature-verification bypass (CWE-347), not withdrawn or rejected.
Source-to-sink at v1.4.0: forged structurally valid host JWT -> VerifyHostToken ignores ParseWithClaims error and token.Valid -> Authorize err==nil -> GET /api/v1/host HostPull disclosure.

BIC is the repository root 0bacbd9f6c0b7a4516443fe62b47ee5a71b6b7ee first-write of VerifyToken's `if token != nil` acceptance; subsequent moves/renames and the 2023 host API are not first-writes of that check.
31e81342fbb83d0b2e4fd3b5b8f60bdc337ee251 fixed the same anti-pattern for VerifyUserToken only, leaving the node/host verifier vulnerable through to the 2026 NM-258 fix.

Direct fix is 5309aa70d464ef565911369714d661a61481a79b; first public git tag containing it is v1.5.1. Tag/release v1.5.0 (6b7d33fa7749c87e6b3c59b1a544d80c727c478b, 2026-02-11) still has the vulnerable check; the advisory/Zyenra 'patched in v1.5.0' claim conflicts with those exact objects.
